mentl/8bd1ff5:
The previous pin banked a probe: which of region_tracker's three install
sites broke when the handler gained a config parameter? The answer is
none of them. It is the handler's own state initializer reading the
config, and four marches with one variable each pin it exactly.

  no config param                                  clean
  param present, unread by the initializer         clean
  param read inline, list_filled(buckets, [])      trap 134
  param read through a call, region_index_new(b)   trap 134

Not the presence of the parameter, not the nested call, not the value
passed — 65536 at every site is behaviour-identical to the working form
and traps exactly as 1024 did — and not capture versus literal, since
both trap. The read is the defect.

The symptom fits the documented class at a new site. branch_bracket's
own comment names install-config-capture-read, "a capture-referencing
config arg reads 0", for arm bodies. The same zero arriving in a state
init explains the trap mechanically: list_filled(0, []) is an empty
index, len(idx) - 1 is -1, i32_and(handle, -1) is the raw handle, and
list_set runs off the end.

It has never fired because no handler in the wheel derives state from
its config. graph_handler assigns one straight through and works;
intern_table uses a literal. Deriving is the untested shape, so the
medium accepts such a handler and miscompiles it — type-checks and
traps, which is the class §0 exists to make unsayable.

Nothing landed deliberately. A gate for this is red by construction, and
red gates do not land; the fixture and the substrate fix are one
landing. The experiment reverted whole.
mentl/8b3028a:
graph_emitfn_at built its by-name index at first demand and latched

emitfns_idx_covers is the column length the index was folded from. Equal

a miss cannot tell absent from stale, so it re-derives on every absent

mentl/8bdcba9:
Two layout primitives. Reindent-on-compose: every interior renders at
depth zero and each enclosing block indents its whole interior exactly
once at composition, so depth is never threaded and never wrong —
nesting depth is composition depth. The fixed two-space literals had
rendered a nested match's arms at column 2 at any depth; the probe now
shows depth-correct nesting four levels down. Six wrappers recomposed:
block, match, effect decl, handler decl, vertical variants, prose-else.

Fits-or-breaks: an inline render survives when it is one line within
the 100-column budget, else the construct takes its block layout — fn
and let break after the equals with the body indented, an overflowing
if takes the cuddled-block vertical through render_branch_block, an
overflowing call breaks one argument per line, and a long prose-free
variant set takes the vertical layout. The budget measures at depth
zero, the honest approximation stated at the fits_inline site.

Formatted non-comment lines over 100 columns fell 1,335 to 628 against
an authored baseline of 568, idempotent-all-50 held at every rung, and
the march ran clean through all three pins of the arc.

mentl/8b7d9be:
Bank the adversarial verification of the multi-shot producer (band B) and
add the non-identity lowering gate.

The re-execution driver is evidence-proven sound through boot (the re-run's
perform resolves to the innermost replay, co-performed effects pass to the
outer handler, no re-entry) BUT only as a pre-inference DESUGAR, never a
lower-time synthesis: the replay handler must be REGISTERED so the op is
non-singleton, or Tier-1 singleton dispatch re-reads the driver's own state
global and re-enters it. The direct-driver is correct only for mn-multishot's
exact shape; the general form needs op-args, per-resume state, and accepts
the effectful-prefix re-duplication the native-cont O(1) path avoids.

The fixpoint is "safe by classifier-gap," not by construction: the wheel's
own backtrack (search.mn:134) and Synth.enumerate_inhabitants
(synth_proposer.mn:131) are genuine multi-shot handlers misclassified OneShot
by the tail-recursion-resume-cardinality gap. Completing the classifier would
fire the new lowering on the wheel and break the fixpoint unless the general
driver is built — so the two must co-land as one desugar. Shipping the narrow
driver now greens one micro and is a band-aid; don't.

tests/native-cont/twice-handler-nonidentity.mn gates the non-identity
lowering (body pick()+3, arm sums two resumes, want 36; dormant 13 today).

mentl/8b285c1:
The self-hosted type checker now tracks which algebraic effects
each expression performs — matching the Rust checker's capability.

- EffRow ADT: EfPure | EfClosed(List) | EfOpen(List, Int)
- merge_effects: union effect rows through sub-expressions
- infer_expr returns 5-tuple: (type, subst, counter, reason, effects)
- TFun(params, ret, effs): functions carry their effect signature
- type_to_string: shows 'with IO, State' for effectful functions
- list_union/list_contains: set operations for effect merging

Programs are typed effect graphs. The checker proves it.

Lays the Phase 12 networking scaffolding — the testable parts. The
exit criteria (two real devices on different networks complete a
full match, brief blip reconnection, long-disconnect forfeit) are
operator-verified per `SIGNALING.md`; CI cannot exercise them
without a real signaling server in the loop.

Cycle 1 — net crate + ggrs<->matchbox bridge:
  * Workspace member `crates/net` was a stub from Phase 0; this
    populates it.
  * `matchbox_socket = "0.14"` without its `ggrs` cargo feature —
    that feature pins `ggrs ^0.11` and we ship on `bevy_ggrs = "=0.21"`
    which pulls `ggrs ^0.12`. Same dep-version trap that motivated
    cutting bevy_roll_safe in Phase 11; same playbook (own the
    ~50 LOC of bridge code rather than fork or downgrade).
  * `net::MatchboxBridge` — newtype wrapper around `WebRtcChannel`,
    impls `ggrs::NonBlockingSocket<PeerId>` via bincode-encoded
    messages over the channel's send/receive primitives. Mirrors
    matchbox's reference impl byte-for-byte at the wire so
    compatibility with their `ggrs` feature is incidental but
    preserved.
  * `encode_message` / `decode_packet` helpers exposed pub for the
    app crate's matchbox driver to reuse.
  * 2 unit tests: trait-impl compile-fence, PeerId thread-through.
    The wire-format round-trip can't be tested in a unit context
    (`ggrs::Message` has private fields in 0.12) — the round-trip
    is implicitly exercised when peers exchange a real sync
    handshake at runtime.
